title: Prediction Equations for Marathon Performance: A Systematic Review
authors: Keogh A, Smyth B, Caulfield B, Lawlor A, Berndsen J, Doherty C
journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
population: 36 observational studies containing 114 marathon prediction equations
findings: 36 studies with 114 equations; 61 based on training and anthropometric variables, 53 requiring laboratory tests or equipment.
r2 reported for 68 equations (r2 = .10-.99) and SEE for 19 equations (0.27-27.4 min).
Course gradient, sex and expected weather were often omitted; some widely used equations reported no r2.
Heterogeneity precludes identifying a single best equation; runners should be wary of relying on one.
limitations: Heterogeneous accuracy metrics prevented pooling; study quality not summarised in the abstract; not specific to training volume.
implications: Do not rely on one published equation; present a predicted time range from several sources (recent race or time trial, training-based estimates).
Add course profile, sex and expected temperature as explicit adjustments.

verification.notes: Crossref title, journal, first author, issued 2019-10 match; abstract re-fetched and numbers match.
